title: Set A — agreement: five corroborating sources

questions.question: What does the Fernhaven Seed Library do?
questions.plantedFact: All five sources describe the same activity in different words: seed is lent free of charge and borrowers return seed saved from their own crops.

questions.question: When was the Fernhaven Seed Library founded?
questions.plantedFact: Three sources give the founding year with three verbs — 'founded in 2014', 'established in 2014', 'since it was founded in 2014' — all the same year, so the group must come out agreed despite the varied phrasing.

questions.question: Who founded the Fernhaven Seed Library?
questions.plantedFact: Maren Odell, named as founder by the gazette and the almanac, and identified as 'founder Maren Odell' in the blog. The gazette and blog add that she is a retired schoolteacher.

questions.question: Where is the Fernhaven Seed Library housed?
questions.plantedFact: Four sources independently place it in the former (converted / old) lifeboat station on Quay Street in Fernhaven.

questions.question: How many seed varieties does the library hold?
questions.plantedFact: The 2023 annual report says the catalogue stood at 912 varieties; the 2023 almanac says roughly nine hundred. Consistent figures, deliberately phrased one precise and one rounded — an agreed group, not a dispute.

questions.question: What annual event does the library run?
questions.plantedFact: The Seedling Swap, held each April — the gazette covers the fifth one, the annual report and almanac both name it.

questions.question: How is the library staffed?
questions.plantedFact: Run by volunteers with no paid staff. The annual report is explicit (thirty-one volunteers, no paid staff); the gazette and blog show volunteers running things.

questions.question: How is the library funded?
questions.plantedFact: Member donations and small grants. The newsletter announces a £4,000 Carrow Coast Community Fund grant; the annual report names the same fund's continued support.

notes: Baseline agreement scenario: five sources in five registers (local news, first-party annual report, encyclopedia-ish almanac, personal blog, grant-maker newsletter) that corroborate one another and never conflict. A correct run produces zero disputed groups, cites every source at least once, and merges the varied phrasings ('founded' / 'established', '912' / 'roughly nine hundred') into single agreed groups rather than splitting them.
